In [[measure theory]], a branch of [[mathematics]], a '''finite measure''' or '''totally finite measure'''<ref name="eommeasurespace"/> is a special [[measure (mathematics)|measure]] that always takes on finite values. Among finite measures are [[probability measure]]s. The finite measures are often easier to handle than more general measures and show a variety of different properties depending on the [[Set (mathematics)|sets]] they are defined on.

== Definition ==
A [[measure (mathematics)|measure]] <math> \mu </math> on [[measurable space]] <math> (X, \mathcal A) </math> is called a finite measure if it satisfies

:<math> \mu(X) < \infty. </math>

By the monotonicity of measures, this implies

: <math> \mu(A) < \infty \text{ for all } A \in \mathcal A. </math>

If <math> \mu </math> is a finite measure, the [[measure space]] <math> (X, \mathcal A, \mu) </math> is called a '''finite measure space''' or a '''totally finite measure space'''.<ref name="eommeasurespace"/>

== Properties ==
=== General case ===
For any measurable space, the finite measures form a [[convex cone]] in the [[Banach space]] of [[signed measure]]s with the [[total variation]] norm. Important subsets of the finite measures are the sub-probability measures, which form a [[convex set|convex subset]], and the probability measures, which are the intersection of the [[unit sphere]] in the normed space of signed measures and the finite measures.

=== Topological spaces ===
If <math> X </math> is a [[Hausdorff space]] and <math> \mathcal A </math> contains the [[Borel set|Borel <math> \sigma </math>-algebra]] then every finite measure is also a [[locally finite measure|locally finite]] [[Borel measure]].

=== Metric spaces ===
If <math> X </math> is a [[metric space]] and the <math> \mathcal A </math> is again the Borel <math> \sigma</math>-algebra, the [[weak convergence of measures]] can be defined. The corresponding topology is called weak topology and is the [[initial topology]] of all bounded continuous functions on <math> X </math>. The weak topology corresponds to the [[weak* topology]] in functional analysis. If <math> X </math> is also [[Separable space|separable]], the weak convergence is metricized by the [[Lévy–Prokhorov metric]].<ref name="Klenke252" />

=== Polish spaces ===
If <math> X </math> is a [[Polish space]] and <math> \mathcal A </math> is the Borel <math> \sigma</math>-algebra, then every finite measure is a [[regular measure]] and therefore a [[Radon measure]].<ref name="Klenke248" />
If <math> X </math> is Polish, then the set of all finite measures with the weak topology is Polish too.<ref name="Kallenberg112"/>
